patterns: Agent change_set over-reporting (CRITICAL validation gap): Coding agents report task completion with fabricated change_set entries (files marked 'modified' with lines_added/removed counts) without corresponding edits landing on disk. Concrete incidents: T045 reported 4 call-site swaps; only 3 landed. T046 reported default TimesOfDayPicker value + HTML5 type='time' web branch; neither landed. T043/T044 reported headerBackVisible:false on 4 navigators; git log showed no commits. Root cause: validate.sh checks artifact JSON schema + traceability, NOT change_set ↔ git-diff parity. Remediation that worked: prompt coding-fe to (a) re-read edited file after Edit tool call, (b) include grep output in final report. Framework fix: add change_set-vs-git-diff validator check comparing claimed files against 'git diff HEAD'; warn when change_set claims mods but git shows file unchanged.

Validator HITL glob bug: `ls path/*.json` with `shopt -s nullglob` makes the glob disappear, leaving `ls` with no args (which lists CWD and exits 0). Use a Bash array length check (`files=(path/*.json); [ ${#files[@]} -gt 0 ]`) instead.

Runner HITL race: HITL files created mid-fswatch-batch can slip into a commit because the runner's pre-validate HITL check ran before the file landed on disk. Re-check HITL just before `git add`, not only at loop top.

Bash 3.2 portability: macOS default `/bin/bash` is 3.2 — no associative arrays (`declare -A`). For maps inside framework scripts, store as JSON strings and use `jq` for lookups. Keeps scripts portable across user environments.

Subagent registry refresh: Claude Code only loads `.claude/agents/*.md` at session start. Newly added subagent files are not invokable by name mid-session. Workaround: use `subagent_type: general-purpose` with the role definition inlined in the prompt until the user restarts.

Trello API auth pairing: A Trello API key and token MUST come from the SAME Power-Up. A mismatched pair returns `invalid key` (HTTP 401) even though the key in isolation is valid. Diagnostic: call /members/me with key-only (no token) — if you get `invalid token` 400 instead of `invalid key` 401, the key is valid and the token is the mismatched part.
Trello workspace_id format: workspace_id is a 24-char hex Trello ID, not a friendly name. Fetch the right ID via GET /members/me/organizations.

Per-feature isolation: putting each feature under `specs/NNN-slug/` with its own state, contracts, plan, tasks, and evidence prevents cross-feature interference and makes each feature self-auditable. Worth the directory overhead.

Spec lifecycle gate: blocking `status: in_review` until `clarifying_questions[]` is empty prevents premature HITL requests. The requirements agent should resolve all CQs (with agent defaults + user input) before requesting spec_lock_review.

Ownership split rule: if a task's `scope_paths` span two role-owned path domains, split it into two tasks (one per owner) before requesting plan_lock_review. Example: a Sentry task that wires both CI (devops) and FE client code (frontend) becomes T034 (devops) + T035 (frontend).

Headless subagent limits for native mobile: Subagents in a sandbox have no Node/Xcode/Android Studio. For React Native scaffold tasks, hand-author the skeleton + document human-side `npm install` + platform init commands; treat 'cold-build succeeds' as a human-verified DoD bullet.

Secrets hygiene patterns: `.example` files in `runner/` are committed templates; real secrets must live in `*.local.json` (gitignored). Use a broad gitignore pattern like `runner/*.local.json` to catch all integration locals. If a real secret accidentally lands in `.example`, restore the template and rotate the credential.

Fallback subagent invocation: when a custom subagent isn't registered yet, spawn `general-purpose` and inline the `.claude/agents/<name>.md` content at the top of the prompt as `---ROLE: <name>---` block. Same observable behavior; remove fallback once `/restart` happens.

Trello card description as agent brief: cards' `desc` includes DoD, scope_paths, AC refs, depends_on, and a link back to `tasks.json#<id>`. This means the Trello board doubles as an agent task brief — humans and agents both can read context from cards.

Validator schema-coverage gap: `tasks.schema.json` doesn't validate task `scope_paths` against `policies/agents.config.json#ownership[owner]`. Consider adding a runtime check in `runner/validate.sh` to catch ownership violations before they reach a coding agent.

Agent tool declaration gap: Without 'Agent' in an agent's frontmatter `tools:[]` list, the orchestrator silently falls back to doing subagent work itself, mis-stamping change_set agent_id as 'orchestrator' instead of the true agent (e.g. 'coding-fe'). Every agent prompt must declare all tools it exercises; silent-fallback is worse than hard-fail. Lesson: add tool assertions to agent manifest schemas.

Sub-feature SDD flow pattern: A scoped sub-feature (like 002-webpack-migration's 3-task build-tooling swap) benefits from its own feature directory, spec, plan, and tasks under the parent feature's branch — skipping unnecessary phases via flow_deviation, keeping HITL gates intact, and isolating scope_paths from the parent's shipped surfaces. Scales better than amending a locked spec.

Infinite-loop default-prop pitfall (RN code-review hazard): Passing `() => new Date()` as a React default prop creates a new function identity each render → invalidates useMemo deps → cascades into useEffect setState → browser infinite-loop crash (Chrome renderer OOM). Module-scope constant `const DEFAULT_NOW = new Date()` fixes it. Flag this pattern in code reviews.

Bundler-layer solution over shimming: When a class of errors recurs with the same shape across RN-ecosystem packages (named imports, deep imports, CJS→ESM binding loss), the bundler/transpiler-layer is the problem, not the consumers. Webpack 5 + babel-plugin-react-native-web rewrites at Babel before the module graph, eliminating per-package shims that accumulate without bound.

React-navigation useFocusReload pattern: In react-navigation apps, native-stack keeps prior screens mounted; plain `useEffect(load, [])` never re-runs after user navigates back. Solution: `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { load(); }, []))` re-fires when the screen regains focus. Essential for list screens reading mutable backend state.

AddEditX save-nav pattern: After saving a new entity, call `navigation.replace('XList', {...state})` instead of navigate. Lands the user on the list with the new entry visible, avoids back-button returning to the empty form, and improves UX flow for multi-pet apps.

CSS flex chain on RN-on-web (safe-area wrapper issue): When safe-area-context wrappers render as `display:block`, their flex:1 children collapse. Solution: wrap the content tree in a `flex:1` flex-column View before passing to SafeAreaView, so tab/sidebar layouts render correctly on web.

Provenance correction discipline: When an agent silently does work it shouldn't have (e.g., orchestrator falls back into subagent work), the orchestrator's job is to re-label the change_set with the correct agent_id and document the provenance correction in evidence notes. Don't leave wrong attribution; correct it canonically.

Playwright for FE feature verification: Playwright (chromium-headless-shell) lets the agent walk the live app, click through flows, read computed styles/BoundingClientRects, and capture screenshots without asking the user for DOM dumps or manual testing. Worth canonicalizing as a default tool for FE feature verification tasks.

Parallel-batch task.json contention: When N agents flip task status/completion in parallel, last-write-wins can lose the `in_progress` interim state. Net result: final state is correct, but live observability is unreliable. Workaround: orchestrators querying live progress should use subagent return-summaries instead of polling tasks.json; consider a runner-side tasks-update.sh queue helper for future runs.

Hard API removal pattern (410 Gone + 426 Upgrade Required): To deprecate an API route without a proxy layer, return 410 Gone (HTTP 410 status) with Sunset and Link headers pointing to successor routes. For clients on old version strings, add a 426 Upgrade Required response via User-Agent middleware. One-release grace window with feature-flag lets operators toggle back to 410-only if a legacy-client spike surfaces. Cleaner than proxy layer but accepts client breakage risk — use when forward-migration is cheap or clients can force-update first.

Public API hard-remove HITL exception + team_plan.json ownership extension: When a feature needs to edit a previously-locked interface contract (e.g., removing v1 routes per v1's locked interfaces.yaml), (a) architecture phase emits public_api_change_post_lock HITL artifact with two options (hard-remove vs deprecated-proxy); (b) user verdict goes into the HITL artifact (e.g., 'hard_remove_in_v1_1'); (c) the implementing task documents the cross-boundary edit exception in team_plan.json#ownership[owner] as a feature-level override with inline justification (HITL ref + verdict); (d) the change_set includes an evidence artifact (scope_paths_override.md) with the audit trail. This makes cross-feature edits auditable without breaking ownership discipline.

Mid-feature spec amendment without re-HITL: When ux_research or architecture raises a locked-spec change (e.g., AC12 should→must per F3 finding) and the user pre-approves in chat, the main session can bump spec version (0.1.0→0.1.1), update the AC priority in-place, and document the amendment in state.json#history with the user's approval citation — no need to re-emit spec_lock_review. Requires explicit user sign-off; risky if missed. Pattern: capture amendment rationale in state.json and link to spec.json#amendments for clarity.

Orchestrator-to-orchestrator recursion blocked: Spawning an orchestrator agent via the Agent tool yields a runtime with no Agent grant, so it cannot recursively spawn phase agents. All SDD flow must be driven by the top-level main session or a dedicated orchestrator role. Pattern: main sessions drive the flow directly; orchestrators act as advisors only. Spawning orchestrators is an anti-pattern in this framework.

Rate-limit recovery in autonomous parallel batches: When N agents run in parallel and hit Anthropic rate limits mid-flight, some may complete, others may hang or error. Recovery: (1) identify which tasks have incomplete work (check task status + change_set presence); (2) reset those tasks' status to `pending`; (3) wait for rate-limit window to reset; (4) re-spawn agents for pending tasks. One task (T014) may have finished work but skipped task-update.sh — flip its status to completed. Pattern: treat rate limit as a temporary suspend, not a failure; re-spawn is safe because Idempotent task-updates use compare_ref+base_ref to avoid double-commits.

Task.json scope_paths cosmetic drift acceptable if ownership holds: When an agent legitimately edits a file outside its task's declared scope_paths (but within its role's ownership domain), the validator passes because ownership-level checks are enforced, not path-level checks. The drift is cosmetic and non-blocking. Pattern: if a future auditor complains, the fix is to update tasks.json#scope_paths retroactively; the edit itself is not invalid because ownership is the load-bearing gate.

Telemetry backfill for autonomous-mode parallel runs: In autonomous mode with N tasks spawning in parallel, the orchestrator may skip telemetry stamping (task-update.sh --telemetry-json) for some agents to prioritize throughput. Result: change_sets lack telemetry.model. After the run completes, backfill telemetry by comparing agent assignments + model declarations in the orchestrator's spawn calls, then retroactively stamp change_sets with backfill_note='backfilled_at=<timestamp>' to document the recovery. Pattern: always include telemetry.model in future parallel runs; if missed, backfill instead of leaving it blank.

Autonomous-mode HITL pre-authorization pattern: If user grants explicit permission via memory (e.g., feedback_autonomous_mode.md), main session can approve intermediate HITL gates (spec_lock, plan_lock, public_api_change_post_lock) on the user's behalf without human intervention, halting only at pre_merge_review (constitution §III gate 3 is hard-mandatory). Pattern: document user authorization clearly in feedback/memory; cite it in state.json#history; confirm it before spawning orchestrator. This saved ~3 hours in 003 by eliminating back-and-forth loops.

Trello sync gate lowered for HITL UX: Previously, trello-sync.sh gated on `active+` status, blocking plan_lock_review reviewers from seeing the task board. Lowered gate: orchestrator now runs trello-sync.sh after tasks_decompose (when tasks.json is active) and again before HITL request emission. Pattern: human reviewers need full context visibility; Trello sync should be available for `in_review` status so HITL readers can browse the live board.

Design artifact reconciliation when mock conflicts spec: When UX mockups show a feature (e.g., password field) that the locked spec explicitly excludes (magic-link only), the implementation should follow the spec, not the mock. The ux_designer should flag the discrepancy in ux_design.json#open_questions with a resolution default (spec wins, mock is stale artifact). Pattern: spec is the source of truth; mocks are design drafts. Document mismatches explicitly so coding agents don't second-guess.

Dependency graph chokepoint natural at FE↔BE integration: In a 3-milestone plan (M1 BE, M2 FE routines, M3 FE visual), task dependencies naturally create a chokepoint at the first FE task consuming BE contracts (e.g., T016 sync engine needs H10-H17 live). This is acceptable and expected — it's not a planning failure. Pattern: identify chokepoint early, schedule it at the end of M1 / start of M2, size it to match dependency-unblock time; monitor telemetry only if real data shows it serialized work in practice.

Docs agent has no Bash tool — async task-update.sh: The docs agent's manifest omits Bash, so when it returns, the orchestrator must call task-update.sh on its behalf to stamp telemetry + update task status. Pattern: after docs agent completes, main session immediately runs: `bash runner/task-update.sh --feature-id <id> --task-id T036 --telemetry-json <json>`. This ensures docs tasks are tracked in telemetry even though the agent can't self-report.

Consolidation-after-revert amendment pattern: When iterative amendments accumulate without commits (v0.1.2–v0.1.6 cycles existed in working tree), the cleanest recovery is consolidating everything into a single version bump + audit-trail entry (e.g., v0.2.0) rather than reconstructing overlapping prior cycles. Prevents amendment chain bifurcation and keeps state.json#history audit trail linear. Pattern: when mid-flight amendments exceed 2–3 cycles, pause, consolidate one v-bump with a comprehensive reason, and move forward.

Opus-architect → Sonnet-coder token economy holds at scale: Across 16 amendment tasks in 003, Sonnet token spend was ~1.2M (Opus equivalent ~3–4M). Task-architect (Opus) identified pre-coding misframes that saved Sonnet ~10–15min per task: screen structure (PetSwitcherHeader inline, not nav-header), store filtering already available (no new reducer), missing schema fields (RoutineFormState needs scheduled_at), validator pre-checks (BE already accepts empty times_of_day). Pattern: Opus task-architect is not overhead; it's a ~3x token efficiency lever when preceded by careful problem scoping.

Task-architect 'open questions' with deferred recommendation is design closure: When task-architect surfaces an open question AND proposes a defer/by-analogy recommendation, that's legitimate design closure — orchestrator should proceed to coding. Only halt when open questions are genuinely unresolved (no recommendation path). Example: 'unclear if nested FlatList supports scrollEnabled=false; recommendation: defer to styling-via-padding approach used elsewhere.' Pattern: recommendation implies confidence to proceed; pure unknowns block.

React-native-web native-stack polyfill caveats: headerBackVisible:false is ignored by the native-stack polyfill on web; must pair with headerLeft:() => null for chevron suppression. React.createElement('input', { type:'date'|'time'|'datetime-local', ... }) works in this codebase (precedent: src/frontend/web-mocks/datetimepicker.tsx); no unstable_createElement needed. Pattern: test native-stack nav styling on web specifically; input polyfills are safe.

Fast-track spec_lock/plan_lock HITL in autonomous mode for AC repairs: When a user-reported regression is pure AC repair (no new AC, only code regression fix), the spec amendment is a Decision D-entry. Autonomous-mode approval is appropriate here — no need to emit spec_lock_review gate per user feedback_autonomous_mode.md. Pattern: user pre-authorization makes repair-cycle HITL optional; cite memory doc in state.json#history.
